headline: Mechanistic models test which features bacterial regulation and metabolism require
label: Mechanistic Modeling Of Regulatory Systems
summary: Mechanistic models of bacterial translation, heat shock response, and catabolic metabolism are being used to identify which regulatory features drive observed…
synthesis: The dominant thread is mechanistic interpretation of quantitative models of bacterial regulation, in which models are examined for the features they require to reproduce or explain behavior. A mechanistic ODE model of E. coli translation initiation predicts a shift from complex-limited to ribosome-limited behavior across growth conditions. A model of the E. coli heat shock response integrates protein folding with σ32 regulation and identifies synergies and trade-offs among feedforward control, chaperone sequestration and degradation. What is new is the explicit use of such models to resolve which mechanistic components matter. A catabolic net-conversion study extends this framework to metabolic network stoichiometry, computing net conversions via elementary flux modes and introducing a thermodynamic analysis. The items differ in maturity, with one published study and two preprints, so the metabolic work represents an extension rather than a shared result.
